reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that fluorine treatment on Ti-45Al-8.5Nb alloys promotes a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale and reduces oxidation mass gain at 1000 °C, supporting the key premises. However, the evidence is limited to TiAl intermetallics, not refractory high-entropy alloys, so the extrapolation to a different alloy class is a gap in direct support.
premises: Fluorine treatment promotes formation of a protective Al2O3 scale on Al-containing alloys
The Al2O3 scale significantly reduces oxidation mass gain
The Al2O3 scale is continuous and adherent
The mechanism involves fluorine-induced Al enrichment at the surface
